Subject: Re: NewShore pilot recap — kickoff notes

Thanks for the call earlier — this is Sara from NewShore. Quick summary from our side:

- We're piloting an auto-summarization + entity extraction flow for support tickets (avg ticket length ~ 1.2k tokens).
- 95th latency target for live routing: <= 350ms.
- Monthly inference budget target: ~$12k for initial pilot.
- Primary concerns: quality regression vs on-prem-like isolation for PII.

Action items for us: share a small anonymized prompt set and two weeks of sample tickets (done; attached).

Questions that came up:
1) Which model families do you recommend for latency-sensitive summarization with strong entity fidelity?
2) How aggressive can we be on quant (AWQ/GPTQ/FP8) before we hit noticeable entity drop?

Appreciate the guidance — Sara

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: NewShore pilot recap — recommended next steps

Sara — thanks for the samples and the clear constraints, this helps a lot. Recap and our proposed path forward below.

Recap (from our discovery):
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 350ms (US region).
- Cost target: ~$12k/month for pilot (approx 1.5M tokens monthly).
- Quality sensitivity: entity extraction recall > 92% baseline.

Recommended pilot plan (high level):
1) Model shortlist: Llama2-13B-Chat (FP16 baseline), Mistral-Instruct-7B (AWQ-4), and a trimmed mix with Falcon-40B-compat (GPTQ-2 medium). Rationale below.
2) Benchmarks: We'll run the attached microbenchmarks and token-accuracy sweep on your prompt set (see linked Drive).
3) Quantization trade study: run three arms — AWQ (aggressive 4-bit), GPTQ (medium, layerwise calibration), FP8 fast path on supported infra. We'll pair accuracy probes (entity F1) with tail-latency measurements.
4) Private pilot options: Redwood Dedicated pool in us-west with VPC peering if needed for PII.

Initial model recommendations (short):
- Mistral-Instruct-7B (AWQ-4): best latency/cost for short summaries; good instruction-following but verify entity fidelity on long tickets.
- Llama2-13B-Chat (FP16): higher base quality and entity layering; higher cost/latency but safer on recall-sensitive extractions.
- Falcon-40B-compat (GPTQ medium): middle ground if Llama2 latency is too high — tends to preserve entities better than very aggressive AWQ in our experience.

Quant tradeoffs (quick note):
- AWQ (4-bit): large wins on throughput and cost; can introduce subtle hallucination/skew on rare named entities — we recommend A/B validation vs your dev prompts before rollout.
- GPTQ: more conservative; per-layer calibration preserves more of the logits distribution for rare tokens at the cost of extra tuning time.
- FP8: hardware dependent; can match FP16 quality for many workloads but currently less predictable across GPU generations.

Next steps and owners:
- Redwood: run benchmark sweep on your prompt-set (Evelyn + Monica) — deliver initial accuracy/latency matrix in 3 business days.
- NewShore: provide any additional edge-case tickets and mark high-priority entities (Sara) — target by EOD 2027-05-26.
- Commercial: Aditya will share a pilot pricing sketch + Dedicated option pricing (Aditya).

I attached a baseline bench CSV from a quick run and the prompt set you're already sent. We'll call out any regression modes and recommended rollback options (model variants, fallback to FP16 Llama2).

Would you like a short 30-minute follow-up mid-week to walk the benchmark results?

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Solutions — Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0124

Subject: Re: NewShore pilot recap — model tradeoffs and pilot pricing

Hi Sara / team — quick commercial and pragmatic notes following Evelyn's technical plan.

Pricing sketch for a 6-week pilot (estimated):
- Hosted API baseline (mixed models): ~$9k — fits within pilot target if AWQ arm dominates.
- Dedicated small pool (reserved burst): ~$15k/month but gives tighter latency at 95th and isolation for PII; can be temporarily reserved for the pilot window.

Operational suggestions:
- Start with a two-arm pilot: AWQ-Mistral (cost-first) vs Llama2-13B (quality-first). Measure: entity F1 & 95th latency per prompt bucket.
- Run calibration benchmark for GPTQ on a subset (10% of samples) to estimate tuning time — typically 1–2 business days for a 13B model with our tooling.
- If FP8 hardware is available on your side, we can add a FP8 arm but we'll need to gate on hardware generation notes (we can detect in the job).

Questions for NewShore to confirm pricing/ops:
1) Can you confirm whether on-prem or VPC peering is required for data (PII)?
2) Expected token volume during pilot (ballpark) — you flagged ~1.5M/month earlier; confirm.

I'll attach the pilot pricing draft and a short SOW — happy to iterate.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
